P1 — Full objective does not identify relative semantic orientation — Counterevidence: Useful orientations can occur from optimization bias or additional constraints, and the result does not prove failure of every published fit. The later release uses affine query/key layers, so invariance is asserted for the written linear Eq.(11), not all affine source configurations. More common anchors cannot break the proved paper-objective sign symmetry.
P2 — Released losses change targets and relative weighting — Counterevidence: Original source version and experiment configuration unknown; no observed optimization collapse

P2 — Released losses change targets and relative weighting — Counterevidence: Code 1-Gram constants cancel in differences and are not defects themselves. data/get_dataset.py globally normalizes mobility counts, agreeing with averaged trips; no false missing-mobility-normalization issue retained. Permitted zero projections show a source objective degeneracy but do not demonstrate actual training collapse.
